rows.notes: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.A commercial electricity average for Texas (8.66 cents/kWh in June 2026) used as a Houston proxy (CenterPoint TDU service area commercial plans range from ~6.35 to 12.5 cents/kWh all-in depending on load factor and contract). Labeled as Texas commercial proxy.

Houston-area retail solar buyback plan (e.g., Green Mountain Energy Pollution Free Solar or Chariot Energy FIT plans operating in CenterPoint TDU). Typical fixed export buyback is ~8.5 cents/kWh; wholesale-indexed or credit-capped plans range from 2.5 to 12 cents/kWh. Commercial eligibility differs from residential: commercial net-billing/buyback requires specific interval metering (IDR/AMS) and commercial retail contracts, often with monthly net-surplus zeroing or lower export credit caps than residential plans.

EPA eGRID2024 ERCOT All (ERCT) total output emission factor published in 2026 GHG Emission Factors Hub: 700.7 lb CO2/MWh. Converted to kg CO2/kWh by multiplying by 0.00045359237 (700.7 * 0.00045359237 = 0.319 kg CO2/kWh). Strict CO2 output factor (does not include CH4, N2O, or global warming potentials for CO2e).

NREL PVWatts annual production for Houston, TX (ZIP 77002 area) for a standard commercial rooftop system. Typical specification: 10 kW DC system size, 20-degree tilt, 180 degrees azimuth (due south), 14.0% system losses, 1.2 DC-to-AC ratio yields ~1,580 kWh/kW/year (range 1,450 to 1,700 kWh/kW/yr depending on roof tilt, azimuth orientation, and soiling/shading losses).

Office energy use intensity. Expressed as site electricity in kWh/ft2/year. National median site EUI for office from CBECS/ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager converted to site electricity equivalent (~52.9 kBtu/ft2/yr site total ≈ 15-18 kWh/ft2/yr electrical portion). Total site energy includes electricity and natural gas.

Retail energy use intensity in kWh/ft2/year (site electricity). CBECS/Portfolio Manager median retail site EUI (~51.4 kBtu/ft2/yr site total). Retail properties feature high lighting and plug-load intensities.

Industrial / warehouse energy use intensity in kWh/ft2/year (site electricity). Unrefrigerated warehouses average ~6.6 kWh/ft2/yr, whereas refrigerated cold storage facilities exceed 28.8 kWh/ft2/yr. Industrial category differences reflect process loads and refrigeration.

Multi-family commercial energy use intensity in kWh/ft2/year (site electricity). Multi-family residential properties differ from commercial offices due to tenant-paid vs. master-metered configurations, heavy domestic hot water loads, and 24/7 occupancy profiles.

rows.item: Probability solar project starting now qualifies before deadline
rows.source_url: https://www.irs.gov / IRS Notice 2024-XX / IRA statutory transition rules
rows.notes: Probability solar project starting now qualifies before deadline: Under IRA statutory rules, projects beginning construction before July 5, 2026 are subject to specific transition guidelines or grandfathering provisions regarding prevailing wage and apprenticeship (PWA) requirements or domestic content rules. For a project beginning construction as of November 14, 2026, full compliance with statutory PWA rules is strictly mandatory to secure the 30% base ITC. Analyst judgment probability is 0.95 assuming professional legal and engineering controls ensure PWA compliance.
